packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-14 - unverified image-only reading

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE STATEMENT
- Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this fragment. This is a blind reading.
- Beyond the stated rules: I listed the packet directory to learn image filenames (packet.json not opened). No web, search, edition or catalogue consulted.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- image-001 (overview): a small single parchment slip, c. 16.5 cm wide by c. 6.5 cm tall (cm scale below), with faint vertical fold lines. Four lines of text in brown ink in the upper middle; generous blank margins all round, and the rest of the slip blank. The text looks complete as it stands (starts with an enlarged initial and ends with a punctus followed by blank space); nothing visible is cut off.
- image-002 = left half at native resolution; image-003 = right half; they overlap in the middle (words "un", "tempest-", "Femes", "p(ri)nches" appear in both).
- Script: a rather informal gothic book hand/cursive, brown ink. Enlarged, flourished initial "N" at the start of l.1 (same ink, no colour). Punctus used as separators between clauses. Tironian "et" (written like "7") used twice. One superscript "i" above "p" in l.4 (abbreviation). No rubrics, glosses or later annotations visible.
- Language: vernacular, apparently French (Old French / Anglo-Norman type spellings) - observation from the word forms only. Content appears to be a short weather/season forecast (wet winter, dry summer, deaths); interpretation only.

TRANSCRIPTION (physical lines preserved; line numbers per image)
image-002 / image-003 combined (overview image-001):
l.1  Nos aurons d'avan[?] un yver ymbreus c'est a
l.2  dire pluuieus 7 tempestieus . le estet sec .
l.3  le vendenge laboreus . Femes morunt . [?]ees
l.4  pilleront . Bois 7 p(ri)nches[?] morunt .

Per-image line labels:
image-002 l.1  [N]os aurons dawan[?] un      (word 3: "dawan"/"d'avan"/"davan" - the letter after "da" is a w-like form; uncertain)
image-002 l.2  dire pluuieus 7 tempest-
image-002 l.3  le vendenge laboreus . F-      (word 2 could also be "vendenye"/"vendengie"; there is a stroke above the end like an abbreviation or "e" accent)
image-002 l.4  pilleront . Bois 7 p(ri)nche-      (superscript "i" above "p")
image-003 l.1  un yver ymbreus cest a      ("yver": first letter y with long tail; "ymbreus" could be "ymbrens"/"ymbrous"; "cest" has a ligatured st)
image-003 l.2  -mpestieus . le estet sec .
image-003 l.3  -us . Femes morunt . [?]ees      (last word: tall initial with a loop, then "-ees"/"-ecs"; possibly "Plees", "Flees", "Brees"; unresolved)
image-003 l.4  p(ri)nches morunt .      (expansion of "p" + superscript i as "pri" is tentative; could be "prunches")

Separate readings of uncertain letters:
- l.1 "aurons": a-u-r-o-n-s clear.
- l.2 "pluuieus" is written with "uu" (could be read "pluuiens"); "tempestieus" also possibly "tempestiens".
- l.2 "estet" = "e-s-t-e-t" with a ligatured "st"; could be "estez".
- l.3 "morunt" also at l.4: "morunt" (could be "morrunt"); second instance has a small mark under the r.

LIMITATIONS
- The text is short and fully visible; uncertainty is confined to individual letter forms noted above. No damage obscures the text. The reverse of the slip is not shown.
